confirmed_root_causes: PostgreSQL exact and lexical retrieval previously treated the entire query as one substring, causing broad misses.
Structured retrieval previously filtered geography only and returned arbitrary record rows when query constraints were absent.
Router vocabulary did not cover corpus terms such as highest, planned, installed, geotagged, population, and report identity patterns.
Fusion compared incompatible raw relevance scores across retrieval channels, allowing generic structured rows to dominate semantic evidence.
fixes_implemented: Token-aware parameterized exact retrieval across filename, format code, and canonical content.
Token-aware lexical retrieval across canonical content and document metadata.
Structured retrieval query-term coverage across document, record, and canonical fields.
Rank-normalized fusion across exact, structured, lexical, and semantic channels.
Qdrant client 1.19 query_points compatibility and canonical content_unit_id mapping.
remaining_issue: Production PostgreSQL field/source coverage and fusion still fail to preserve expected evidence for most cases; Q015 regressed after rank-normalized fusion. Further changes require dedicated diagnosis, not score tuning.
